scholarships.title: UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) - Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative
scholarships.official_source: UNHCR (funded by the Government of Germany, with support from the Governments of Denmark and the Czech Republic and private donors; implemented by UNHCR country operations and DAFI partners such as Windle International)

existing.description: DAFI is UNHCR's dedicated tertiary scholarship programme for refugees and returnees, founded in 1992 and funded principally by the Government of Germany. The published scholarship package covers a range of costs including tuition and study materials, food, transportation and accommodation, and depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner may also cover academic preparatory, language and ICT courses as well as psychosocial support. It funds ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent programmes and ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary and TVET programmes of two years or more, and it explicitly does not cover master's studies. Applications are made through the DAFI Programme Management Platform, which was live and accepting registrations and submissions on 2026-10-01.
eligibility: UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) offers qualified refugee and returnee (in selected countries*) students the possibility to earn an undergraduate degree in their country of asylum or home country

The applicant must be a recognized refugee or, where the country operation accepts them, an asylum seeker living in the country of asylum (published Rwanda wording: 'The applicant must be a recognized refugee or asylum seeker living in Rwanda')

Applicant should have been accepted to a university in the country of asylum; proof of admission must be submitted (published Rwanda wording: 'Applicant should have been accepted to a university in Rwanda. (You will have to submit proof of admission to a university.)')
Priority will be given to those who achieved excellent academic performance (published Rwanda wording)
Only one family member can apply/obtain DAFI scholarship to ensure that benefits allocated are equally given to other refugee students (published Rwanda wording)
Secondary selection criteria: female applicants and persons with special needs education are highly encouraged to apply (published Rwanda wording)
The DAFI Programme aims to provide equal opportunities for women and men (published Tajikistan wording)
existing.eligibility_summary: Recognised refugees and, in selected countries, returnees seeking an undergraduate (ISCED 6) or short-cycle tertiary/TVET (ISCED 5, two years or more) place in their country of asylum or home country, who are not in receipt of another higher-education scholarship.
benefits: The DAFI scholarship programme may also provide academic preparatory, language and information and communication technology (ICT) courses, as well as psychosocial support, depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner
coverage: Academic preparatory courses (depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner)
Language courses (depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner)
Information and communication technology (ICT) courses (depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner)
Psychosocial support (depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner)
requirements: Apply through the DAFI Programme Management Platform at https://unhcr-dafi-tertiary.scholarshipsplatform.com/ - the platform instructs applicants to register an account, start the application (saved in-progress) and submit it for review
DAFI Scholarship programme application is free of charge

The final status of the application is notified by email from the DAFI platform (published Azerbaijan instructions wording: 'Submit your application for review and wait for notification from UNHCR about the final status of your application. The notification should come to your e-mail address from the DAFI platform.')
For any questions about the application process, contact the country office by email using the published country list, or your nearest UNHCR office or DAFI partner
documents: UNHCR Proof of registration (published Rwanda wording: 'Please attach your UNHCR Proof of registration')
Official/certified copy of the high school diploma (published Rwanda wording: 'Please upload your official/certified copy of the high school diploma.')
University admission letter or proof of acceptance for study in a university in the country of asylum (published Rwanda wording)

Equivalence certificate from the Ministry of Education of the country of asylum (published Rwanda wording: 'Please upload the equivalence certificate from the Ministry of Education of the country of asylum')
application_method: Check the call published by your own UNHCR country operation for the current cycle, including its country-specific deadline and any local additions to the criteria
Register an account on the DAFI Programme Management Platform at https://unhcr-dafi-tertiary.scholarshipsplatform.com/
Start the application and save it in-progress
Attach the required documents listed in your country operation's call
Submit the application on the DAFI Programme Management Platform for review
Wait for notification of the final status, which is sent by email from the DAFI platform
existing.selection_notes: The published Rwanda call states that priority will be given to applicants who achieved excellent academic performance, that only one family member may hold a DAFI scholarship, and that female applicants and persons with special needs education are highly encouraged to apply. It also states that only qualified candidates duly registered with UNHCR are invited to interviews, that names of shortlisted candidates are posted at the respective offices, and that academic documents are verified with the relevant authorities (the last two statements are published in the Windle International Kenya DAFI scholarship instructions, not on the UNHCR Rwanda call). The UNHCR programme page states that UNHCR and its education partners closely monitor scholars' academic progress and well-being through regular engagement with students and their institutions.
existing.best_fit: Refugees and returnees recognised by UNHCR who hold a secondary-school qualification and have been admitted to an undergraduate, short-cycle tertiary or TVET place in their country of asylum or home country, and who are not already holding another higher-education scholarship.
existing.notes: The scholarship does not cover master's degree programmes (published: 'DAFI does NOT cover Masters studies.' / 'Please note that the scholarship does not cover master's degree programs.'). Awards are not deferrable, renewable or multi-year by default: funding follows admission to an ISCED 5 or ISCED 6 programme in the cycle applied for. No return-home obligation is published, and because studies take place in the country of asylum or home country no relocation is required. No clinical or field-of-study restriction is published beyond the general rule that the programme targets undergraduate and short-cycle tertiary/TVET study. The 2024 cycle was the first since 2020 with a decrease in the number of scholars supported, reflecting reduced global funding. As this is a multi-country programme with no published global deadline, the applicable deadline is the one published by the applicant's own UNHCR country operation; the published 2026/2027 country windows had all closed by 31 August 2026 at the time of verification, and the platform itself remained live and accepting registrations on 2026-10-01.
existing.duration: Duration follows the degree programme enrolled in: ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent, or ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary / TVET of two years or more
existing.application_period: Country-specific. The 2026/2027 cycle ran on country-published windows in July-August 2026 (Rwanda 15 July-7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 7 July-21 August 2026; Slovakia 1 July-31 August 2026). New country calls for the next cycle are announced on the relevant UNHCR country help page and applications are submitted through the DAFI Programme Management Platform.
existing.deadline_display: No single global deadline is published. Deadlines are set per country operation and published on the UNHCR country help pages (published 2026/2027 examples: Rwanda 7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 21 August 2026; Slovakia 31 August 2026). Applicants must check their own country operation's call.

existing.description: The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships place three Fellows per year for 12 months in the executive offices of the African Development Bank (Abidjan), the UN Economic Commission for Africa (Addis Ababa) or the International Trade Centre (Geneva). Fellows work on research and policy design and receive direct mentorship from the head of the host organisation. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation funds the position; the Foundation's own programme page states a stipend of $100,000. This is a professional work placement, not a degree-granting scholarship, so no tuition is paid.
eligibility: Minimum 7 years' of relevant work experience

Master's degree (minimum) from a recognized institution in banking, business, economics, other social sciences, finance, international development, or another discipline relevant to the host's business
Under the age of 40; or 45 for women with children
Any additional criteria as set by the host organisation
AfDB host route adds: not an active, non-active, retired or separated staff member of the Bank
AfDB host route adds: no close family relations with an active or non-active staff member
AfDB host route adds: government officials, active military personnel and political party leaders are not eligible
existing.eligibility_summary: Nationals of any African country with a minimum master's degree, at least seven years of relevant work experience, and under 40 (45 for women with children).
benefits: Membership of the Mo Ibrahim Foundation's Now Generation Network (NGN) after the Fellowship
coverage: Annual stipend (Foundation states $100,000), paid monthly by the host institution
Foundation-funded travel and shipping costs for assumption of duty and repatriation
All official mission travel expenses, including travel insurance, borne by the host (excluding assumption-of-duty and repatriation travel)
requirements: Apply online through the host organisation's own application system
Submit a comprehensive Curriculum Vitae indicating date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience
documents: Comprehensive CV (date of birth, nationality, education, relevant experience)
application_method: Choose the host organisation route on the Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page
Open the host organisation's vacancy or programme page (AfDB, ITC or UNECA)
Complete the online application form on the host's system
Attach CV, academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation before the host's closing date
existing.selection_notes: The host's Human Resources department vets applications to draw up a shortlist of ten files, which the Foundation then reviews; a shortlist of three candidates is put to the head of the host (for the AfDB route, the President of the Bank or a designate) for final selection. Only applicants who fully meet the requirements and are considered for interview are contacted.
existing.best_fit: African nationals with a master's degree and at least seven years of relevant work experience who want senior-level policy exposure in a continental or multilateral institution.
existing.notes: This is a work placement, not a degree programme: the contract is for one (1) year and is not renewable, and the Fellow is not a regular employee of the host and gains no right to employment. For the AfDB route the Fellow is barred from applying for a staff position at the Bank for one year from the end of the Fellowship. The Fellow is not eligible for the Bank's child educational scheme, staff medical insurance or retirement plans; the Mo Ibrahim Foundation is responsible for ensuring the Fellow arranges their own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan. Applications are routed through three different host systems with potentially different closing dates, so check the host page you intend to use.
existing.application_period: Opened 22 September 2026; closes 20 November 2026 for the 2027 cycle
existing.deadline_display: Applications for the 2027 Fellowships are open until 20 November 2026
